passages.original: Sed priusquam de imperio eius loquar, dicam pauca de moribus, adulescens cum esset Gordianus, de quo sermo est, poemata scripsit, quae omnia exstant, et quidem cuncta illa quae Cicero, id est Marium et Aratum et Alcyonas et Uxorium et Nilum. quae quidem ad hoc scripsit ut Ciceronis poemata nimis antiqua viderentur, scripsit praeterea, quemadmodum Vergilius Aeneidos et Statius Achilleidos et multi alii Alexandriados, ita etiam ille Antoniniados, hoc est Antoninum Pium et Antoninum Marcum versibus disertissimis libris triginta vitam illorum et bella et publice privatimque gesta perscribens.
passages.english: But before I speak of his reign, I will say a few things about his character. When Gordian, of whom we are speaking, was a young man, he wrote poems, all of which survive, and indeed [he wrote on] all those [subjects] that Cicero [did], that is, the *Marius*, the *Aratus*, the *Halcyones*, the *Uxorius* and the *Nilus*. These he wrote precisely so that Cicero's poems might seem too old-fashioned. He wrote besides, just as Vergil [wrote] an *Aeneid*, Statius an *Achilleid*, and many others an *Alexandriad*, so he too [wrote] an *Antoniniad*, that is, [on] Antoninus Pius and Antoninus Marcus, recording in thirty books of most eloquent verse their life, their wars, and their public and private deeds.
passages.notes: 'quidem ad hoc scripsit ut Ciceronis poemata nimis antiqua viderentur' could also be taken as a result clause ('with the result that Cicero's poems seemed too old-fashioned'), but 'ad hoc' points to purpose. The titles Uxorius and Nilus are otherwise little known among Cicero's poems.
